title: Choose Rateboard's look
question: The roll picked The Docket (a shop receipt). Keep it, take an alternative, or ask for a new set.

options.label: The Docket
options.thesis: Every conversion printed as an honest, itemised docket: amount, rate, source, date, margin note.
options.viewport: Amount field on top; the converted total set huge like a receipt TOTAL line; beneath it the itemised provenance lines (rate, rate date, source, mid-market note) with dotted leaders.
options.risk: Could read as a novelty if the paper effects outweigh the numbers.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale alone: the TOTAL is the only large thing on the screen.
No shadowed cards: structure comes from 1px rules and perforation lines only.
All watchlist trend lines share one % scale, so cards compare honestly.

options.label: Boarding Pass
options.lineage: Airline boarding passes and baggage tags
options.thesis: From ⇄ To set like an origin ⇄ destination pass, currency codes huge like airport codes.
options.viewport: AUD → USD as giant codes across a pass; the result on the stub; watchlist as a stack of passes below.
options.risk: Familiar: travel apps lean on this, and it can feel like an airline app.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: The answer hangs like an airport sign: one yellow band, black type, the number monumental.
options.viewport: A yellow band owns the top: amount, then the converted figure monumental; white working area below.
options.case: Travellers know this by heart and it reads instantly; yellow is loud for daily use.
options.risk: Yellow at this scale may tire the eye and fights the green/red trend colours.

options.label: Pocket Timetable
options.thesis: One type size everywhere; rank carried by weight, case and reversal like a printed timetable.
options.viewport: Converter as a reversed carbon plate; watchlist as timetable columns on goldenrod.
options.case: Strong travel identity; the single type size makes the big number impossible, so it loses on clarity.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The number as a giant live specimen.
options.case: Nothing about travel or money; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale alone: the TOTAL is the only large thing.

options.label: Design Annual
options.thesis: Rates as plates on uncoated stock.
options.case: A gallery, not a converter; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Structure from 1px rules, no shadowed cards.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Currencies as plates at a fixed scale.
options.case: No link to the audience; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Every trend line on one shared % scale.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Hides the watchlist and the converter; loses on both axes.
options.kept: On phones the answer owns the first screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech converter, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Amount and currency pickers, big result, list of rates below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every money app by design.
